fieldMarks: Grey/tan body, white lower legs and belly
Black face markings extending down from horn bases; stripe along spine
Slightly curved horns 60-150 cm; 115-125 cm at shoulder
behavior: Nomadic and gregarious, groups averaging 14; males often solitary and territorial
Grazes, browses in drought, digs up to 1 m for tubers and roots
habitat: Stony plains, dunes, rocky hills and arid country.
range: Native to southern Africa; successfully introduced to the southwestern US and Mexico.
